speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I understand you've had knee pain after recently increasing your physical activity. To help me determine the cause, have you experienced any swelling, locking, or giving way of the knee?

speaker: Patient
text: 23-year-old female. The patient presents with knee pain that started yesterday and has been steadily worsening. She cites recent participation in volleyball involving repetitive pivoting and twisting movements as a possible cause. She was advised at her last physical exam that weight loss could be beneficial for her health.

speaker: Doctor
text: That is very helpful; the combination of recent pivoting in volleyball and worsening pain is concerning for a ligament or meniscal injury. Given your history of being advised to lose weight, do you feel your knee is unstable or "gives way" when you try to stand or walk on it? Also, can you point to the exact location of the pain, such as the inner (medial) or outer (lateral) side, or directly under the kneecap?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Knee pain, specifically over the medial aspect of the tibia just inferior to the patella. I also have Recent weight loss attempt, Increased physical activity.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Medial Tibial Stress Syndrome (Shin Splints)

The pain location you described is classic for medial tibial stress syndrome, which often occurs after a rapid increase in activity like volleyball. Have you noticed any focal tenderness specifically along the inner edge of your shin bone (tibia), or does the pain feel more diffuse?
